messages:
Alex: quick flag — after the kernel selection tweak yesterday we're seeing a 9-12% p50 regression on the reranker/embeds non-chat endpoints. Not huge but stable. want to propose a lightweight batch scheduler change to avoid tiny batch formation on high qps spikes.

Priya: ugh. any profiling yet? where is the time going — kernel vs scheduling? :thinking:

Alex: did a flamegraph for the rerank pipeline on cpu->gpu handoff. majority is still in matmul kernels, but there's a bigger-than-expected overhead in dequeue + kv-cache check path when requests are short (avg token=16). flame snippet: `dequeue(12%) -> prepare_inputs(9%) -> copy_kv(6%) -> kernel(58%) -> postprocess(15%)`.

Jamie: note: kv-copy shows up even for non-chat because we materialize empty past for each request right now. that forces an extra memcpy per item. we can short-circuit for rerank/embeds if sequence_length == 1 and no past.

Matt: proposal: continuous-batcher v2: 1) use token-budget target instead of fixed batch-size for non-chat (target_tokens_per_batch = 1024) 2) prefer age-bound queue policy (max-delay=12ms) 3) short-circuit KV copy for no-past requests.

Sara: I ran an A/B with token_budget=1024 and max-delay=12ms on a small cluster. observations: throughput +6%, p50 latency -7% but p99 slightly worse (+3ms) under taily burst. probably due to occasional aggregation with one large request.

Priya: can we add a max-item cap in the token-budget scheduler to avoid one huge request stealing budget? e.g. max_items_per_batch=64. also add per-worker stratification so we don't mix 1-token and 1024-token requests frequently.

Matt: yep. suggested config: `{"target_tokens":1024, "max_items":64, "max_delay_ms":12, "stratify_threshold":64}`. also propose a dequeue heuristic: favor oldest until budget >= 256 tokens then allow size-based greedy.

Alex: sounds good. need to watch for perf regressions post-kernel-change; kernel team rolled a small GEMM micro-optim that changed alignment behavior (faster large mats, slower many small mats). that explains why p50 got worse but p99 OK.

Jamie: quick patch: avoid any memcpy for empty past in `prepare_inputs`. PR incoming. should cut that 6% path.

Sara: experiment plan: rollout token-budget scheduler on 10% traffic for rerank endpoints with the memcpy patch. collect token-distribution histogram, per-batch token variance, and per-worker hotness. target: net p50 <= baseline and throughput >= baseline +4%. I'll schedule the rollout midday tomorrow.

perfbot: PROFILE SUMMARY (1769409999): baseline-run: p50=18.6ms p95=62.4ms p99=120ms; post-kernel-change: p50=20.4ms p95=61.8ms p99=122ms; memcpy-path accounted for ~6% CPU time. recommended actions: short-circuit KV, token-budget batching, cap max-items.

Alex: perfect. if Jamie's memcpy patch lands today i'll freeze kernel backport until we validate the new scheduler. thanks all — let's reconvene after A/B metrics. :thumbsup:
